title: Conservative-credit routing: soft-reserve demotion for free/paid/enterprise
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Design and implement a conservative, credit-preserving routing policy that prioritizes enterprise > paid > free while minimizing downstream quota exhaustion and customer-visible degradations. Introduces soft-reserve buckets, burst smoothing, and predictive demotion to fallback model variants to keep high-tier SLOs intact during spikes.
decisions: Use soft-reserve buckets (configurable fraction of committed credits) per tenant tier instead of hard throttles to reduce head-of-line blocking for enterprise traffic.
Apply an EWMA-based burst score per tenant to trigger temporary demotion to compatible model variants when projected credit depletion within 5 minutes exceeds threshold.
Fallback model variants will be chosen by decreasing cost-per-token while honoring minimum quality thresholds defined in model metadata (quality_score >= 0.75).
Prefer regional-preferring routing: when enterprise reserved capacity exists in-region, route enterprise traffic there even if paid/free are sent to best-effort pools.
Telemetry event schema (routing.decision) will include pre- and post-credit estimates to enable postmortem fairness analysis.
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy deployed behind feature flag and enabled for 5% of global traffic without customer-facing errors.
Enterprise 99th percentile latency remains within 1.2x baseline under 2x traffic spike during canary.
No tenant sees >20% unexpected drop in model quality measured by prompt-set micro-evals for the canary cohort.
Operational dashboard shows per-tier projected credit burn and predicted demotions with alerting when aggressive demotion occurs.
Runbook updated with rollback steps and mitigation (priority queue override and emergency top-up).
